subject: Skyline Analytics — technical follow-up & prompt governance playbook

Subject: Post-demo notes + request for architecture details and next steps

Hi Lucas / Paula —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: integrate Redwood for semantic search + assisted insights in Skyline's analyst UI (low-latency recs, reranking for top-N, and a safe tool-calling layer for on-prem enrichment).
- Immediate asks from Skyline engineering that we heard: SDK onboarding plan, auth model (API keys vs. OIDC), routing for mixed-hosted/private data, and guidance on structured output / tool-calling for enrichment steps.

Can you confirm which environment you want us to target for the POC (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC)? That drives a few of our recommendations. Also if you can share a short list of the top 3 API consumers (product/infra teams) and an engineer we can loop into the technical deep dive, we’ll convert this into a 30–45 minute architecture workshop.

Jasmine from Solutions will propose an initial architecture and a set of prompt templates we recommend we lock down during the POC (versioning and red-team plan included). We’ll attach a preliminary arch sketch before the call.

Next steps proposed:
1) You confirm POC environment and primary contact (reply here) — by EOD Mon 24-May
2) We'll send an architecture draft + prompt template pack — by Tue 25-May
3) Schedule tech workshop (30–45m) to validate architecture and run a quick red-team scoping session — target week of 31-May

Thanks — looking forward to moving this quickly.

—Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + request for architecture details and next steps

Thanks Aditya — good demo. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule the deeper technical session: 

1) POC environment: We want to start on Hosted to iterate fast, but we need a path to Dedicated and Private (VPC) for later stages — we’ll want to validate that your routing/fallback behavior keeps latency acceptable.
2) Auth: We prefer OIDC for long-term, but API keys for the initial POC is OK. Can you outline the migration plan from API keys -> OIDC and whether there are any limitations with private deployments?
3) Structured output: We need strict schemas for entities we extract (account, event, risk_score). How do you track output schema drift and enforce schema compatibility across prompt/template versions?
4) Prompt governance & security: We need a clear approach to prompt versioning, preventing prompt injection, and an outline of a red-team plan (what will you simulate, what tooling do you use).

Also looping in our eng lead Paula — Paula, would you and someone from infra be available for Tue 25 or Wed 26 for the 30–45m session?

—Lucas

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Reed <l.reed@skyline.ai>, Paula Kim <paula.kim@skyline.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + request for architecture details and next steps

Hi Lucas / Paula —

Appreciate the clarifying points. Attached is a lightweight architecture sketch (skyline-arch-draft.png) and an initial prompt templates DOC (prompt-templates-v0.2.md). Below are direct answers and a recommended POC plan.

POC target: Hosted (fast iterate) with a validated migration path to Dedicated / Private. We’ll include explicit compatibility checks in the workshop so you can see routing behavior.

Auth migration:
- Phase 1 (POC): short-lived API keys scoped by project + IP allowlist for quick onboarding.
- Phase 2: OIDC integration (recommended) — Redwood supports OIDC for token minting and role-based routing; we’ll provide an example auth flow (Auth0/Azure AD) and a sample client config.
- Phase 3 (Private): KMS integration for keys and optional HSM support; we’ll document any platform-specific caveats.

Routing & latency controls:
- Policy-based routing: requests tagged by tenant and workload (low-latency vs batch) -> route to Hosted low-latency pool or Dedicated pool.
- Automatic fallback: when Dedicated capacity is saturated we fall back to compatible quantized model in Hosted; config is per-route.

Embeddings & rerankers:
- Use embeddings for candidate retrieval (cos-sim) and a dedicated reranker model for ordering top-10.
- We’ll configure periodic reindexing; embeddings versioning stored alongside prompt template versions to avoid mismatches.

Structured output & schema enforcement:
- Enforce model responses via schema-checker (JSON schema) in the client SDK and server-side post-validators. If schema fails, we flag and route to a human-in-the-loop path or return a structured error.
- Schema drift monitoring: daily sample checks with percentage drift metrics surfaced in Console.

Prompt versioning & governance:
- Each template stored with semantic version (vMAJOR.MINOR.patch), change notes, author, and gating test set (unit prompts).
- CI: prompt templates run against a fixed eval harness on PRs — regressions block merge.
- Rollouts: canary traffic for new templates, automatic rollback on quality threshold breaches.

Prompt injection mitigations:
- Input sanitization: escape or canonicalize untrusted fields; strong recommendations for separating user-provided content into structured fields vs. natural language context.
- System-level policies: prepend immutable system prompt that enforces no-exec/no-credentials, and a runtime guard that checks model output for disallowed tokens/commands.
- Red-team layer: we maintain a catalog of adversarial prompt vectors; during POC we’ll run a small subset against critical templates.

Red-team proposal (POC scope):
- Duration: 1.5 hours during the tech workshop — tabletop + live prompt fuzzing against top 3 templates.
- Deliverables: issue log, exploitable example prompts, remediation steps, and recommended guard rails.

Attachments: skyline-arch-draft.png (flow), prompt-templates-v0.2.md (sample templates + schema examples).

If that looks good, we’ll lock Tue 25 or Wed 26. Best times for our infra/solutions team: Tue 25 between 10–12 PT or Wed 26 between 09–11 PT.

—Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0188

From: Lucas Reed <l.reed@skyline.ai>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes + request for architecture details and next steps

Thanks Jasmine — this looks encouraging. A couple of pragmatic follow-ups before we schedule the red-team workshop: 

- Can you provide 2–3 concrete example prompt templates (with input / expected JSON schema) we can review ahead of the session? We want to validate they won’t leak PII when run against customer transcripts.
- On the "runtime guard" you mention: is that a server-side module we can host in our VPC for Private deployments, or a managed Redwood feature? We need to know what we can audit/replace.
- Please call out any limitations for reranker models in Hosted mode (latency targets for 99th pct).

If you can send the three sample templates + an explicit note on whether the guard is self-hostable, we’ll confirm Wed 26 at 09:30 PT for a 45-minute session and loop in our infra engineer (cc'd).

—Lucas

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Reed <l.reed@skyline.ai>, Paula Kim <paula.kim@skyline.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Skyline POC — confirmed workshop + next steps (templates attached)

Lucas / Paula —

Following up to confirm Wed 26 May at 09:30 PT for the 45-minute architecture + red-team scoping workshop. Agenda and owner notes below: 

1) 09:30–09:40 (Aditya) — business goals & success criteria for POC; finalize primary API consumers and performance targets.
2) 09:40–10:05 (Jasmine) — architecture walkthrough (routing, embeddings + reranker path, schema enforcement).
3) 10:05–10:20 (Jasmine + Lucas) — prompt governance: templates, versioning, and CI gates. Live review of 3 sample templates attached.
4) 10:20–10:30 (Red-team micro-run) — quick adversarial checks against 2 templates; log issues and next actions.

Deliverables after workshop (we will send within 48 hours):
- Updated architecture diagram (skyline-arch-draft.png -> finalized)
- Prompt templates v0.2 with JSON schema and unit tests (prompt-templates-v0.2.md)
- Short red-team report with remediations and recommended guard rails
- Draft SOW for POC (attached SOW-skyline-draft.pdf) — please review and flag commercial questions to Aditya.

Answers to your specific asks:
- We've attached 3 example templates (in prompt-templates-v0.2.md). They include input/expected-output examples and JSON schemas. We also included a quick PII checklist for each template.
- The runtime guard is offered as a managed Redwood feature for Hosted and Dedicated, and as a self-hostable containerized module for Private deployments (we’ll hand over audit logs and rules in the Private package).
- Reranker constraints: Hosted 99th-pct latency target for top-10 rerank is ~220ms under baseline configurations; we'll verify during the POC and can recommend a Dedicated pool if tighter SLOs are required.

Action items (owners):
- Skyline: confirm SOW redlines and legal point-of-contact (Lucas/Paula) — due Thu 3-Jun
- Redwood (Aditya): prepare commercial SOW and finalize trial credits — due Mon 31-May
- Redwood (Jasmine): finalize templates, attach unit tests, and add the red-team harness to the workshop deck — due Wed 28-May
- Schedule: we've requested DocuSign link (see related_links) for SOW signing; HubSpot record created: SKY-2027-04-A.

Thanks all — we’ll see you Wed 26 at 09:30 PT.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0220
